text:
A: Hello.
B: Oh, hello. Can you hear me all right?
A: Yeah, fine. Darren.
B: I'm Alison. Nice to meet you, Darren. Erm, I've never done one of these before, so you'll have to bear with me.
A: Me neither. Not sure what we're meant to talk about, to be honest.
B: No, I don't think they tell you. I suppose just, sort of, whatever comes up. Whereabouts are you?
A: King's Lynn. Norfolk.
B: Oh, right. I'm in Stockton, up in the North East. I've never been to Norfolk, I don't think. Is it nice?
A: That's all right. Flat. You can see the weather coming a long way off.
B: That's what Daniel says about the Barrage of a morning. Sorry, Daniel's my son. I walk along the river most mornings, down by the Tees Barrage, and you can watch the rain coming in over the water before it gets to you.
A: Do you get herons?
B: We do, yes. There's one that stands in the same spot nearly every morning. I've started saying good morning to it, which is probably a bad sign.
A: No, that's fair. I fish the Relief Channel and there's one that follow me up and down. Reckon he think I'm feeding him.
B: Oh, you fish. What do you catch?
A: Bream mostly. Pike in the winter. Or nothing, more often than not. Saturday I sat there six hours and had one little roach.
B: Six hours. You must be very patient.
A: Not really. That's the only place I am patient. At work I'm not.
B: What do you do, if you don't mind me asking?
A: Machine operator. Frozen veg plant. I set up the lines, the blanchers and the packing. Twelve-hour shifts, four on four off. Pea season's coming, so that'll be fifty-odd hours a week. Then I'll be knackered.
B: Twelve hours is a long day. My son's on shifts at a warehouse near Teesport, and I never know whether I'm doing his tea at five or keeping it warm till ten.
A: Yeah. I do mine in tubs on my days off. Chilli, stew. Then that's just microwave it when I get in.
B: That's very organised.
A: Have to be. Nobody else is doing it.
B: No. Erm, I'm retired now. I was a medical secretary at a GP surgery for twenty-seven years, so I'm used to organising. I still keep all my bills in box files with labels on. My daughter laughs at me.
A: Nothing wrong with that. Half the lads at work can't fill a fault log in. You want records, otherwise nobody know what's gone wrong.
B: That's exactly what I used to say to the doctors. If it's not written down, it didn't happen.
A: Right.
B: Do you enjoy it, the factory? Or is that a silly question?
A: Er, I like the machines. I like keeping the line running. The managers I could do without. They come down with a clipboard and no idea.
B: We had a few of those at the practice. Very keen on forms.
A: Yeah, that's the type.
B: Is fishing what you do on your days off, then? Or have you other things on?
A: Fishing. I do my mum's garden. Speedway Wednesday nights if I'm not working.
